description: Hand-collected benchmark comparisons across the two adapter methods trained in this repo, each scored base-model vs checkpoint on the same held-out data-science-assistant eval split. See eval.py for the metric definitions.

benchmarks.label: layer_lora checkpoint-3200
benchmarks.note: Scored against a newer generated dataset version weighted toward code-generation tasks -- not the same eval split as runs 1-3, so its base row is not comparable to theirs.

benchmarks.label: layer_lora checkpoint-7500
benchmarks.note: A later, longer run's checkpoint (step 7500, epoch 4.80), based on checkpoint-3200 and scored on a rebuilt eval split -- the base row moved from 2.4269 to 2.6143, which is only possible if the data changed, since the base model is frozen. Both the weights and the split differ from the checkpoint-3200 entry, so the two compare only through their base-relative deltas and neither variable can be isolated. Its own trainer_state records best_metric 1.1515 at this same step with the early-stopping counter at 0, so the run (max_steps 232000) had not plateaued when the checkpoint was written; the 1.3067 here is from a separate eval pass over a different sample, not that in-training number. code_valid_rate denominators are 26 (3/26 base, 5/26 checkpoint), derived from the reported rates.

benchmarks.label: layer_expand checkpoint-16000
benchmarks.note: Later checkpoint of the same run as README's 'layer_expand checkpoint-11200' (run 7, not itself recorded here since it was only ever captured as a printed eval.sh table) -- same outputs/sft-layer-expand-wide run, same configs/sft_layer_expand.yaml (max_steps 20000), 4800 more steps. eval_loss/perplexity are essentially flat versus checkpoint-11200 (0.0484/1.0496 -> 0.0617/1.0636) despite the extra training, and rouge_l_f1/token_f1 fell (0.6948/0.7014 -> 0.4933/0.5394) even though the base row's own eval_loss/perplexity barely moved (2.7433/15.5388 -> 2.7452/15.5682); its rouge_l_f1/token_f1 did move somewhat (0.0974/0.2323 -> 0.0867/0.2094), most likely from a different random subset of generated examples rather than a split change, since the split-independent loss numbers held steady. Read together: this checkpoint is not an improvement over checkpoint-11200 -- flat teacher-forced loss plus falling free-generation metrics after more training is the signature of a run that has already overfit past its useful point, on top of the leakage/train-eval-overlap check already flagged for checkpoint-11200 given its own near-1.0 perplexity. code_valid_rate and the newly-added repetition_loop_rate both tie exactly with their own base row here, so neither is informative at this sample size.
